chapter: Arriving in New York: the Nest Club and Harlem nightlife
title: Margie, Mary Stafford and Jazzbo, the two-voiced singer
summary: Danny recalls blues singer Mary Stafford, buxom Margie, and little Jazzbo who sang soprano and baritone in the cabaret ups.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: All right. Now, there was Margie Sith(?). Later on there was Mary Stafford. You'll see her name on some records. She made a few records during that time.
Margie Sith(?) was a great big woman, looked something Lizzie (?), a big buxom woman, like you see them opera singers, with a little waist and... And at that time I was...

Yeah. Double-breasted chick. Heh. Well, they had what you call ups. Now, they had this little cat, Jazzbo. You'll see a picture in magazine...in a book of a cabaret scene. I think Tiny Parham is in it in a magazine, one of them history books, of a revue in either the Grand Terrace or the Royal Garden. And there's a little-bitty guy there, Jazzbo, a great entertainer. He could equally sing with two voices, a soprano like a woman, then turn and sing like a baritone, like a man.
Oh yes, yes. I remember that.
There was two. There was another one called Jerry Hall. They were little stunted guys, but they had this great talent.

Well, they had what you'd call ups, one after another one, once the people could get a corps of people in there, maybe ten or fifteen people, they'd put on a show. And there would be one after another. They'd come up, and they'd do... They'd make the rounds with the hustle. They went from table to table. They lingered if the people encouraged them. If they didn't, if the people acted indifferent to them, then they went on to the next table. And you could tell if they could hold an audience. Because when Mattie Hite or Clara Smith hit the floor...
